# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS provides a modern and stable environment.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Prevent interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build-essential, git, cmake, OpenMPI, and CA certificates in a single layer.
# This approach optimizes the image size by reducing layers and cleans up apt cache.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings are crucial for stability and performance in non-HPC-fabric environments (e.g., TCP over Ethernet).
# - Allow running as root, common in single-purpose containers.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic with some container runtimes.
# - Ensure TCP is used for communication and disable Infiniband (openib), which is absent in standard cloud VMs.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the Kripke source from the master branch with submodules, build it with MPI support,
# install the executable to a system path, and then clean up the source code.
# CORRECTED: Changed git branch from 'main' to 'master' which is the correct default branch.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git --branch master --depth 1 . && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake for a Release build and enable MPI.
    # CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX defaults to /usr/local, ensuring the binary is on the PATH.
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
      .. && \
    # Compile the application using all available CPU cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # The 'install' target copies the executable to /usr/local/bin, fulfilling the requirement.
    make install && \
    # Clean up the build directory to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /build

# Set a final working directory for application execution.
WORKDIR /data

# Set the entrypoint to the Kripke executable. This allows users to pass
# arguments directly to the application in their Kubernetes job specifications.
ENTRYPOINT ["kripke.exe"]

# Provide a default command. This will be executed if no other arguments are provided,
# making the image self-documenting and easy to test.
CMD ["--help"]

# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the Kripke proxy application
# using the Flux Operator on a Kubernetes cluster.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run the entire job on a single node as requested.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) for the job.
  # Flux will execute `flux run -n 1 ...` with this value.
  tasks: 1

  # Defines the container that runs the application workload.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to execute within the container, wrapped by `flux run`.
      # Kripke is run with no parameters as specified.
      command: kripke
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation, providing better error feedback.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the Kripke proxy application
# using the Flux Operator on a Kubernetes cluster.
# This version corrects issues from a previous attempt.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) for the job.
  # Set to 64 for the experiment.
  tasks: 64

  # Defines pod-specific configurations.
  # The nodeSelector is placed here to correctly target specific hardware.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

  # Defines the container that runs the application workload.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Command corrected to use 'kripke.exe' to match the executable in the container,
      # resolving the 'command not found' error.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configurations for the broker and workers.
  flux:
    # Specify the target architecture for the flux view container.
    arch: arm
    # Customize the Flux container image, here for an arm-based system.
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation, providing better error feedback.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

# This manifest corrects two issues from the previous attempt:
# 1. Corrected the executable name from "kripke.exe" to "kripke". The ".exe" suffix is not standard for Linux executables,
#    and the build process in the Dockerfile produces an executable named "kripke". The exit code 127 ("command not found")
#    confirmed this was the primary issue.
# 2. Restructured the pod specification. The nodeSelector was incorrectly placed. For the v1alpha2 API,
#    it must be located at spec.job.pod.spec.nodeSelector to be correctly applied by the Flux operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the cluster.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation, providing better error feedback.
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific configuration. Required for ARM instances.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines the specification for the job's pods.
  job:
    pod:
      spec:
        # Ensures the pod is scheduled on the selected ARM-based instance type.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the proper executable name.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

# This manifest corrects the pod specification path from the previous attempt.
# The `pod` field, containing settings like nodeSelector, is a direct child of `spec`
# for the MiniCluster v1alpha2 CRD, and the `job` field is not valid.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.

  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the cluster.

    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

      launcher: false

  flux:
    arch: arm

steps.result:
Based on the error logs provided, I have identified two issues with the submitted Kubernetes manifest.

1.  **Command Not Found**: The container logs show the error `kripke.exe: No such file or directory` with an exit code of `127`. This indicates that the executable named `kripke.exe` cannot be found in the container's `PATH`. Although the `Dockerfile`'s `ENTRYPOINT` is set to `kripke.exe`, it's common for build systems like CMake to produce binaries without the `.exe` extension on Linux systems. The command should be `kripke`.
2.  **Incorrect Manifest Structure**: The `backoffLimit` and `pod` specifications (containing `nodeSelector` and `restartPolicy`) are placed directly under `spec`. For the `flux-framework.org/v1alpha2` `MiniCluster` custom resource, these fields should be nested under `spec.job` to correctly configure the underlying Kubernetes Job.

I have corrected these issues in the following manifest.

```yaml
# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for running Kripke.
# 1. Fixed the executable name in the command from "kripke.exe" to "kripke"
#    to resolve the "No such file or directory" error (exit code 127).
# 2. Restructured the manifest to place `backoffLimit` and `pod` specs
#    under the `job` key, as required by the MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size is the number of pods for the MiniCluster.
  size: 1
  # Tasks is the total number of MPI ranks.
  tasks: 64
  logging:
    strict: true
  cleanup: false

  # Application container to run.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # Corrected executable name. The error "kripke.exe: No such file or directory" indicates
    # the binary is likely named 'kripke' on the Linux file system.
    command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
    launcher: false

  # Flux RESTful API settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # JobSpec to control the underlying Kubernetes Job.
  job:
    # Limit retries to 1. If it fails once, it will not be retried.
    backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Select the ARM-based instance type for this workload.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
        # Do not restart pods on failure so logs can be inspected.
        restartPolicy: Never
```

result.item:
Based on the error logs provided, I have identified two issues with the submitted Kubernetes manifest.

1.  **Command Not Found**: The container logs show the error `kripke.exe: No such file or directory` with an exit code of `127`. This indicates that the executable named `kripke.exe` cannot be found in the container's `PATH`. Although the `Dockerfile`'s `ENTRYPOINT` is set to `kripke.exe`, it's common for build systems like CMake to produce binaries without the `.exe` extension on Linux systems. The command should be `kripke`.
2.  **Incorrect Manifest Structure**: The `backoffLimit` and `pod` specifications (containing `nodeSelector` and `restartPolicy`) are placed directly under `spec`. For the `flux-framework.org/v1alpha2` `MiniCluster` custom resource, these fields should be nested under `spec.job` to correctly configure the underlying Kubernetes Job.

I have corrected these issues in the following manifest.

```yaml
# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for running Kripke.
# 1. Fixed the executable name in the command from "kripke.exe" to "kripke"
#    to resolve the "No such file or directory" error (exit code 127).
# 2. Restructured the manifest to place `backoffLimit` and `pod` specs
#    under the `job` key, as required by the MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size is the number of pods for the MiniCluster.
  size: 1
  # Tasks is the total number of MPI ranks.
  tasks: 64
  logging:
    strict: true
  cleanup: false

  # Application container to run.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # Corrected executable name. The error "kripke.exe: No such file or directory" indicates
    # the binary is likely named 'kripke' on the Linux file system.
    command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
    launcher: false

  # Flux RESTful API settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # JobSpec to control the underlying Kubernetes Job.
  job:
    # Limit retries to 1. If it fails once, it will not be retried.
    backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Select the ARM-based instance type for this workload.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
        # Do not restart pods on failure so logs can be inspected.
        restartPolicy: Never
```

# The executable built by the Dockerfile is named "kripke," not "kripke.exe."

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2

metadata:

spec:
  cleanup: false
  # Set size to 1 to run on a single node

    backoffLimit: 1

#    restartPolicy are placed directly under `spec.pod`.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # FIX: Changed executable to 'kripke' to resolve "No such file or directory" error.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific settings for the ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Set restart policy to Never to inspect logs of failed pods.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Select the ARM-based Graviton instance for the job.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This manifest incorporates the final corrections based on previous failures.
# 1. The executable name is set to 'kripke.exe' to resolve the "command not found" error.
# 2. The pod specification (nodeSelector, restartPolicy) is correctly placed
#    directly under `spec.pod`, which is the valid path for the v1alpha2 MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance type.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the 'kripke.exe' executable name.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy to preserve pod logs after failure.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Node selector to target the specific ARM instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

result.item:
Based on the error logs provided, I have identified two issues with the submitted Kubernetes manifest.

1.  **Command Not Found**: The container logs show the error `kripke.exe: No such file or directory` with an exit code of `127`. 2.  **Incorrect Manifest Structure**: The `backoffLimit` and `pod` specifications (containing `nodeSelector` and `restartPolicy`) are placed directly under `spec`. For the `flux-framework.org/v1alpha2` `MiniCluster` custom resource, these fields should be nested under `spec.job` to correctly configure the underlying Kubernetes Job.

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This manifest incorporates the final corrections based on previous failures.
# 1. The executable name is set to 'kripke.exe' to resolve the "command not found" error.
# 2. The pod specification (nodeSelector, restartPolicy) is correctly placed
#    directly under `spec.pod`, which is the valid path for the v1alpha2 MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance type.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the 'kripke.exe' executable name.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy to preserve pod logs after failure.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Node selector to target the specific ARM instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

Based on the error logs provided, I have identified two issues with the submitted Kubernetes manifest.

1.  **Command Not Found**: The container logs show the error `kripke.exe: No such file or directory` with an exit code of `127`. This indicates that the executable named `kripke.exe` cannot be found in the container's `PATH`. Although the `Dockerfile`'s `ENTRYPOINT` is set to `kripke.exe`, it's common for build systems like CMake to produce binaries without the `.exe` extension on Linux systems. The command should be `kripke`.
2.  **Incorrect Manifest Structure**: The `backoffLimit` and `pod` specifications (containing `nodeSelector` and `restartPolicy`) are placed directly under `spec`. For the `flux-framework.org/v1alpha2` `MiniCluster` custom resource, these fields should be nested under `spec.job` to correctly configure the underlying Kubernetes Job.

I have corrected these issues in the following manifest.

```yaml
# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for running Kripke.
# 1. Fixed the executable name in the command from "kripke.exe" to "kripke"
#    to resolve the "No such file or directory" error (exit code 127).
# 2. Restructured the manifest to place `backoffLimit` and `pod` specs
#    under the `job` key, as required by the MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size is the number of pods for the MiniCluster.
  size: 1
  # Tasks is the total number of MPI ranks.
  tasks: 64
  logging:
    strict: true
  cleanup: false

  # Application container to run.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # Corrected executable name. The error "kripke.exe: No such file or directory" indicates
    # the binary is likely named 'kripke' on the Linux file system.
    command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
    launcher: false

  # Flux RESTful API settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # JobSpec to control the underlying Kubernetes Job.
  job:
    # Limit retries to 1. If it fails once, it will not be retried.
    backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Select the ARM-based instance type for this workload.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
        # Do not restart pods on failure so logs can be inspected.
        restartPolicy: Never
```

Looking at the provided Dockerfile, the application binary is installed as `kripke.exe`, but the `MiniCluster` manifest attempts to execute `kripke`.

# This MiniCluster manifest deploys the Kripke proxy application
# using the Flux Operator on a Kubernetes cluster.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run the entire job on a single node as requested.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) for the job.
  # Flux will execute `flux run -n 1 ...` with this value.
  tasks: 1

  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation, providing better error feedback.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

# This manifest incorporates the final corrections based on previous failures.
# 1. The executable name is set to 'kripke.exe' to resolve the "command not found" error.
# 2. The pod specification (nodeSelector, restartPolicy) is correctly placed
#    directly under `spec.pod`, which is the valid path for the v1alpha2 MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance type.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the 'kripke.exe' executable name.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy to preserve pod logs after failure.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Node selector to target the specific ARM instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

result.item:
Based on the error logs provided, I have identified two issues with the submitted Kubernetes manifest.

1.  **Command Not Found**: The container logs show the error `kripke.exe: No such file or directory` with an exit code of `127`. This indicates that the executable named `kripke.exe` cannot be found in the container's `PATH`. Although the `Dockerfile`'s `ENTRYPOINT` is set to `kripke.exe`, it's common for build systems like CMake to produce binaries without the `.exe` extension on Linux systems. The command should be `kripke`.
2.  **Incorrect Manifest Structure**: The `backoffLimit` and `pod` specifications (containing `nodeSelector` and `restartPolicy`) are placed directly under `spec`. For the `flux-framework.org/v1alpha2` `MiniCluster` custom resource, these fields should be nested under `spec.job` to correctly configure the underlying Kubernetes Job.

I have corrected these issues in the following manifest.

```yaml
# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for running Kripke.
# 1. Fixed the executable name in the command from "kripke.exe" to "kripke"
#    to resolve the "No such file or directory" error (exit code 127).
# 2. Restructured the manifest to place `backoffLimit` and `pod` specs
#    under the `job` key, as required by the MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size is the number of pods for the MiniCluster.
  size: 1
  # Tasks is the total number of MPI ranks.
  tasks: 64
  logging:
    strict: true
  cleanup: false

  # Application container to run.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # Corrected executable name. The error "kripke.exe: No such file or directory" indicates
    # the binary is likely named 'kripke' on the Linux file system.
    command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
    launcher: false

  # Flux RESTful API settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # JobSpec to control the underlying Kubernetes Job.
  job:
    # Limit retries to 1. If it fails once, it will not be retried.
    backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Select the ARM-based instance type for this workload.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
        # Do not restart pods on failure so logs can be inspected.
        restartPolicy: Never
```

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS provides a modern and stable environment.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Prevent interactive prompts during package installation.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build-essential, git, cmake, OpenMPI, and CA certificates in a single layer.
# This approach optimizes the image size by reducing layers and cleans up apt cache.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings are crucial for stability and performance in non-HPC-fabric environments (e.g., TCP over Ethernet).
# - Allow running as root, common in single-purpose containers.
# - Disable shared memory mechanisms that can be problematic with some container runtimes.
# - Ensure TCP is used for communication and disable Infiniband (openib), which is absent in standard cloud VMs.
RUN echo "btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism = none" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "btl = ^openib" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf && \
    echo "orte_base_help_aggregate = 0" >> /etc/openmpi/openmpi-mca-params.conf

# Set a temporary working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the Kripke source, build it with MPI support, install the executable, and clean up.
# Note: Using 'master' branch as 'main' does not exist in the repository.
# --recursive is required to fetch the BLT submodule used by the build system.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git --branch master --depth 1 . && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake for a Release build and enable MPI.
    # CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX defaults to /usr/local, ensuring the binary is on the PATH.
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
      .. && \
    # Compile the application using all available CPU cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # The 'install' target copies the executable to /usr/local/bin, fulfilling the requirement.
    make install && \
    # Clean up the build directory to minimize final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /build

# Set a final working directory for application execution.
WORKDIR /data

# Set the entrypoint to the Kripke executable. This allows users to pass
# arguments directly to the application in their Kubernetes job specifications.
ENTRYPOINT ["kripke.exe"]

# Provide a default command. This will be executed if no other arguments are provided,
# making the image self-documenting and easy to test.
CMD ["--help"]

The error `PodInitializing` combined with the series of pod recreation events strongly suggests that the pods cannot start successfully. This is often due to a mismatch between the node architecture and the container architecture, especially for the `flux-view` init container which sets up the environment. The provided manifest does not specify a node to run on, leaving the pod to be scheduled on any available node. If an ARM node is chosen by the scheduler, the default x86_64 `flux-view` init container will fail, leading to the `PodInitializing` error and subsequent pod recreation attempts.

To fix this and optimize performance as requested, I will select the most powerful CPU instance available, the `hpc7g.16xlarge` (64-core ARM), and configure the MiniCluster specifically for it. This includes setting the node selector, specifying the ARM architecture for Flux, providing the correct ARM-based image for the Flux init container, and scaling the task count and application parameters to fully utilize the node's resources. I will also add the requested `backoffLimit` and `restartPolicy`.

```yaml
# This manifest fixes the pod initialization error by explicitly selecting a node
# and ensuring all components (Flux init container, application) match the
# node's ARM architecture. It also optimizes for the "Grind Time Figure of Merit"
# by selecting the most powerful CPU instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) and scaling
# the application parameters to utilize all 64 cores.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster (1 node).
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks, set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance.
  tasks: 64
  # Ensure the pod is not cleaned up on completion to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: "arm"
    # This specific container image is required for the Flux broker on ARM nodes.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Specification for the main application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Command is optimized for a 64-task run to maximize the Figure of Merit.
      # --procs defines the MPI process grid (4x4x4 = 64).
      # --zones increases the problem size per task.
      # --nest GZD is a performance optimization for data layout.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # The main container does not need to launch flux.
      launcher: false
  
  # Specification for the underlying Kubernetes Job and Pods created by the Flux Operator.
  job:
    spec:
      # Set backoffLimit to 1 to prevent retries on persistent failures.
      backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Set restartPolicy to Never to inspect logs of failed pods.
        restartPolicy: Never
        # Selects a specific AWS instance type to ensure architecture compatibility and performance.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
```

result.item:
Based on the error logs provided, I have identified two issues with the submitted Kubernetes manifest.

1.  **Command Not Found**: The container logs show the error `kripke.exe: No such file or directory` with an exit code of `127`. This indicates that the executable named `kripke.exe` cannot be found in the container's `PATH`. Although the `Dockerfile`'s `ENTRYPOINT` is set to `kripke.exe`, it's common for build systems like CMake to produce binaries without the `.exe` extension on Linux systems. The command should be `kripke`.
2.  **Incorrect Manifest Structure**: The `backoffLimit` and `pod` specifications (containing `nodeSelector` and `restartPolicy`) are placed directly under `spec`. For the `flux-framework.org/v1alpha2` `MiniCluster` custom resource, these fields should be nested under `spec.job` to correctly configure the underlying Kubernetes Job.

I have corrected these issues in the following manifest.

```yaml
# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for running Kripke.
# 1. Fixed the executable name in the command from "kripke.exe" to "kripke"
#    to resolve the "No such file or directory" error (exit code 127).
# 2. Restructured the manifest to place `backoffLimit` and `pod` specs
#    under the `job` key, as required by the MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size is the number of pods for the MiniCluster.
  size: 1
  # Tasks is the total number of MPI ranks.
  tasks: 64
  logging:
    strict: true
  cleanup: false

  # Application container to run.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # Corrected executable name. The error "kripke.exe: No such file or directory" indicates
    # the binary is likely named 'kripke' on the Linux file system.
    command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
    launcher: false

  # Flux RESTful API settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # JobSpec to control the underlying Kubernetes Job.
  job:
    # Limit retries to 1. If it fails once, it will not be retried.
    backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Select the ARM-based instance type for this workload.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
        # Do not restart pods on failure so logs can be inspected.
        restartPolicy: Never
```

Based on the error logs, the root cause of the failure is `start failed: kripke: No such file or directory`. The container's log shows an exit code of `127`, which reinforces that the command specified was not found.

Looking at the provided Dockerfile, the application binary is installed as `kripke.exe`, but the `MiniCluster` manifest attempts to execute `kripke`.

The fix is to correct the command in the application container spec to use the correct executable name, `kripke.exe`. Additionally, the fields `backoffLimit` and `pod` were placed incorrectly in the top-level spec; they should be nested under a `job` field according to the MiniCluster specification.

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  size: 1

    backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        nodeSelector:

    # FIX: Corrected command to 'kripke.exe' which is the actual executable name.
    command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
    launcher: false

  # Job spec for pod scheduling and lifecycle policies.

    spec:

    pod:

The error `PodInitializing` combined with the series of pod recreation events strongly suggests that the pods cannot start successfully. This is often due to a mismatch between the node architecture and the container architecture, especially for the `flux-view` init container which sets up the environment. The provided manifest does not specify a node to run on, leaving the pod to be scheduled on any available node. If an ARM node is chosen by the scheduler, the default x86_64 `flux-view` init container will fail, leading to the `PodInitializing` error and subsequent pod recreation attempts.

To fix this and optimize performance as requested, I will select the most powerful CPU instance available, the `hpc7g.16xlarge` (64-core ARM), and configure the MiniCluster specifically for it. This includes setting the node selector, specifying the ARM architecture for Flux, providing the correct ARM-based image for the Flux init container, and scaling the task count and application parameters to fully utilize the node's resources. I will also add the requested `backoffLimit` and `restartPolicy`.

```yaml
# This manifest fixes the pod initialization error by explicitly selecting a node
# and ensuring all components (Flux init container, application) match the
# node's ARM architecture. It also optimizes for the "Grind Time Figure of Merit"
# by selecting the most powerful CPU instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) and scaling
# the application parameters to utilize all 64 cores.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster (1 node).
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks, set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance.
  tasks: 64
  # Ensure the pod is not cleaned up on completion to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: "arm"
    # This specific container image is required for the Flux broker on ARM nodes.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Specification for the main application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Command is optimized for a 64-task run to maximize the Figure of Merit.
      # --procs defines the MPI process grid (4x4x4 = 64).
      # --zones increases the problem size per task.
      # --nest GZD is a performance optimization for data layout.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # The main container does not need to launch flux.
      launcher: false
  
  # Specification for the underlying Kubernetes Job and Pods created by the Flux Operator.
  job:
    spec:
      # Set backoffLimit to 1 to prevent retries on persistent failures.
      backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Set restartPolicy to Never to inspect logs of failed pods.
        restartPolicy: Never
        # Selects a specific AWS instance type to ensure architecture compatibility and performance.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
```

steps.result:
Based on the provided error logs and manifest, I have identified two primary issues.

1.  **Incorrect Executable Name:** The error message `start failed: kripke: No such file or directory` and the corresponding exit code `127` clearly indicate that the command `kripke` cannot be found within the application container's `PATH`. Reviewing the Dockerfile shows that the installed executable is named `kripke.exe`, as specified in the `ENTRYPOINT`. The `command` in the MiniCluster spec must be changed to match this name.
2.  **Malformed Manifest Structure:** The `pod` specification, which includes the `nodeSelector`, is placed incorrectly at the top level of the `spec`. For the Flux Operator, pod-specific configurations like `nodeSelector` must be nested under `spec.job.pod.spec`. While the scheduler eventually resolved this, it is syntactically incorrect and caused initial scheduling failures.

Here is the corrected manifest that addresses these issues.

```yaml
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size of the MiniCluster (number of pods)
  size: 1
  # Total number of tasks to run
  tasks: 1
  # Ensure logs are captured
  logging:
    strict: true
  # Do not delete the pods after completion for debugging
  cleanup: false

  # Flux-specific settings for the ARM architecture
  flux:
    arch: "arm"
    # Defines the container that runs the flux broker
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Defines the application container and command
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # FIX: The executable is named 'kripke.exe' per the Dockerfile. The error log
    # "kripke: No such file or directory" confirms the original command was incorrect.
    command: kripke.exe
    # This is the main application container, not a launcher.
    launcher: false

  # Job-specific pod customizations must be nested here.
  job:
    pod:
      spec:
        # FIX: The 'nodeSelector' was misplaced. It is now correctly nested under 'job.pod.spec'.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
```

# This manifest incorporates the final corrections based on previous failures.
# 1. The executable name is set to 'kripke.exe' to resolve the "command not found" error.
# 2. The pod specification (nodeSelector, restartPolicy) is correctly placed
#    directly under `spec.pod`, which is the valid path for the v1alpha2 MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance type.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the 'kripke.exe' executable name.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy to preserve pod logs after failure.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Node selector to target the specific ARM instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

result.item:
Based on the error logs provided, I have identified two issues with the submitted Kubernetes manifest.

1.  **Command Not Found**: The container logs show the error `kripke.exe: No such file or directory` with an exit code of `127`. This indicates that the executable named `kripke.exe` cannot be found in the container's `PATH`. Although the `Dockerfile`'s `ENTRYPOINT` is set to `kripke.exe`, it's common for build systems like CMake to produce binaries without the `.exe` extension on Linux systems. The command should be `kripke`.
2.  **Incorrect Manifest Structure**: The `backoffLimit` and `pod` specifications (containing `nodeSelector` and `restartPolicy`) are placed directly under `spec`. For the `flux-framework.org/v1alpha2` `MiniCluster` custom resource, these fields should be nested under `spec.job` to correctly configure the underlying Kubernetes Job.

I have corrected these issues in the following manifest.

```yaml
# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for running Kripke.
# 1. Fixed the executable name in the command from "kripke.exe" to "kripke"
#    to resolve the "No such file or directory" error (exit code 127).
# 2. Restructured the manifest to place `backoffLimit` and `pod` specs
#    under the `job` key, as required by the MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size is the number of pods for the MiniCluster.
  size: 1
  # Tasks is the total number of MPI ranks.
  tasks: 64
  logging:
    strict: true
  cleanup: false

  # Application container to run.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # Corrected executable name. The error "kripke.exe: No such file or directory" indicates
    # the binary is likely named 'kripke' on the Linux file system.
    command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
    launcher: false

  # Flux RESTful API settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # JobSpec to control the underlying Kubernetes Job.
  job:
    # Limit retries to 1. If it fails once, it will not be retried.
    backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Select the ARM-based instance type for this workload.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
        # Do not restart pods on failure so logs can be inspected.
        restartPolicy: Never
```

result.item:
The error `PodInitializing` combined with the series of pod recreation events strongly suggests that the pods cannot start successfully. This is often due to a mismatch between the node architecture and the container architecture, especially for the `flux-view` init container which sets up the environment. The provided manifest does not specify a node to run on, leaving the pod to be scheduled on any available node. If an ARM node is chosen by the scheduler, the default x86_64 `flux-view` init container will fail, leading to the `PodInitializing` error and subsequent pod recreation attempts.

To fix this and optimize performance as requested, I will select the most powerful CPU instance available, the `hpc7g.16xlarge` (64-core ARM), and configure the MiniCluster specifically for it. This includes setting the node selector, specifying the ARM architecture for Flux, providing the correct ARM-based image for the Flux init container, and scaling the task count and application parameters to fully utilize the node's resources. I will also add the requested `backoffLimit` and `restartPolicy`.

```yaml
# This manifest fixes the pod initialization error by explicitly selecting a node
# and ensuring all components (Flux init container, application) match the
# node's ARM architecture. It also optimizes for the "Grind Time Figure of Merit"
# by selecting the most powerful CPU instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) and scaling
# the application parameters to utilize all 64 cores.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster (1 node).
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks, set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance.
  tasks: 64
  # Ensure the pod is not cleaned up on completion to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: "arm"
    # This specific container image is required for the Flux broker on ARM nodes.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Specification for the main application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Command is optimized for a 64-task run to maximize the Figure of Merit.
      # --procs defines the MPI process grid (4x4x4 = 64).
      # --zones increases the problem size per task.
      # --nest GZD is a performance optimization for data layout.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # The main container does not need to launch flux.
      launcher: false
  
  # Specification for the underlying Kubernetes Job and Pods created by the Flux Operator.
  job:
    spec:
      # Set backoffLimit to 1 to prevent retries on persistent failures.

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This manifest incorporates the final corrections based on previous failures.
# 1. The executable name is set to 'kripke.exe' to resolve the "command not found" error.
# 2. The pod specification (nodeSelector, restartPolicy) is correctly placed
#    directly under `spec.pod`, which is the valid path for the v1alpha2 MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance type.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the 'kripke.exe' executable name.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy to preserve pod logs after failure.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Node selector to target the specific ARM instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

Based on the error logs provided, I have identified two issues with the submitted Kubernetes manifest.

1.  **Command Not Found**: The container logs show the error `kripke.exe: No such file or directory` with an exit code of `127`. This indicates that the executable named `kripke.exe` cannot be found in the container's `PATH`. Although the `Dockerfile`'s `ENTRYPOINT` is set to `kripke.exe`, it's common for build systems like CMake to produce binaries without the `.exe` extension on Linux systems. The command should be `kripke`.
2.  **Incorrect Manifest Structure**: The `backoffLimit` and `pod` specifications (containing `nodeSelector` and `restartPolicy`) are placed directly under `spec`. For the `flux-framework.org/v1alpha2` `MiniCluster` custom resource, these fields should be nested under `spec.job` to correctly configure the underlying Kubernetes Job.

I have corrected these issues in the following manifest.

```yaml
# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for running Kripke.
# 1. Fixed the executable name in the command from "kripke.exe" to "kripke"
#    to resolve the "No such file or directory" error (exit code 127).
# 2. Restructured the manifest to place `backoffLimit` and `pod` specs
#    under the `job` key, as required by the MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size is the number of pods for the MiniCluster.
  size: 1
  # Tasks is the total number of MPI ranks.
  tasks: 64
  logging:
    strict: true
  cleanup: false

  # Application container to run.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # Corrected executable name. The error "kripke.exe: No such file or directory" indicates
    # the binary is likely named 'kripke' on the Linux file system.
    command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
    launcher: false

  # Flux RESTful API settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # JobSpec to control the underlying Kubernetes Job.
  job:
    # Limit retries to 1. If it fails once, it will not be retried.
    backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Select the ARM-based instance type for this workload.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
        # Do not restart pods on failure so logs can be inspected.
        restartPolicy: Never
```

result.item:
The error `PodInitializing` combined with the series of pod recreation events strongly suggests that the pods cannot start successfully. This is often due to a mismatch between the node architecture and the container architecture, especially for the `flux-view` init container which sets up the environment. The provided manifest does not specify a node to run on, leaving the pod to be scheduled on any available node. If an ARM node is chosen by the scheduler, the default x86_64 `flux-view` init container will fail, leading to the `PodInitializing` error and subsequent pod recreation attempts.

To fix this and optimize performance as requested, I will select the most powerful CPU instance available, the `hpc7g.16xlarge` (64-core ARM), and configure the MiniCluster specifically for it. This includes setting the node selector, specifying the ARM architecture for Flux, providing the correct ARM-based image for the Flux init container, and scaling the task count and application parameters to fully utilize the node's resources. I will also add the requested `backoffLimit` and `restartPolicy`.

```yaml
# This manifest fixes the pod initialization error by explicitly selecting a node
# and ensuring all components (Flux init container, application) match the
# node's ARM architecture. It also optimizes for the "Grind Time Figure of Merit"
# by selecting the most powerful CPU instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) and scaling
# the application parameters to utilize all 64 cores.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster (1 node).
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks, set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance.
  tasks: 64
  # Ensure the pod is not cleaned up on completion to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: "arm"
    # This specific container image is required for the Flux broker on ARM nodes.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Specification for the main application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Command is optimized for a 64-task run to maximize the Figure of Merit.
      # --procs defines the MPI process grid (4x4x4 = 64).
      # --zones increases the problem size per task.
      # --nest GZD is a performance optimization for data layout.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # The main container does not need to launch flux.
      launcher: false
  
  # Specification for the underlying Kubernetes Job and Pods created by the Flux Operator.
  job:
    spec:
      # Set backoffLimit to 1 to prevent retries on persistent failures.
      backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Set restartPolicy to Never to inspect logs of failed pods.
        restartPolicy: Never
        # Selects a specific AWS instance type to ensure architecture compatibility and performance.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
```

result.item:
Based on the provided error logs and manifest, I have identified two primary issues.

1.  **Incorrect Executable Name:** The error message `start failed: kripke: No such file or directory` and the corresponding exit code `127` clearly indicate that the command `kripke` cannot be found within the application container's `PATH`. Reviewing the Dockerfile shows that the installed executable is named `kripke.exe`, as specified in the `ENTRYPOINT`. The `command` in the MiniCluster spec must be changed to match this name.
2.  **Malformed Manifest Structure:** The `pod` specification, which includes the `nodeSelector`, is placed incorrectly at the top level of the `spec`. For the Flux Operator, pod-specific configurations like `nodeSelector` must be nested under `spec.job.pod.spec`. While the scheduler eventually resolved this, it is syntactically incorrect and caused initial scheduling failures.

Here is the corrected manifest that addresses these issues.

```yaml
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size of the MiniCluster (number of pods)
  size: 1
  # Total number of tasks to run
  tasks: 1
  # Ensure logs are captured
  logging:
    strict: true
  # Do not delete the pods after completion for debugging
  cleanup: false

  # Flux-specific settings for the ARM architecture
  flux:
    arch: "arm"
    # Defines the container that runs the flux broker
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Defines the application container and command
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # FIX: The executable is named 'kripke.exe' per the Dockerfile. The error log
    # "kripke: No such file or directory" confirms the original command was incorrect.
    command: kripke.exe
    # This is the main application container, not a launcher.
    launcher: false

  # Job-specific pod customizations must be nested here.
  job:
    pod:
      spec:
        # FIX: The 'nodeSelector' was misplaced. It is now correctly nested under 'job.pod.spec'.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
```

Based on the error logs provided, the key issue is `flux-shell[0]: FATAL: task 0 (host kripke-minicluster-0): start failed: kripke: No such file or directory` with an exit code of `127`. This indicates that the executable named `kripke` could not be found within the application container's PATH.

Reviewing the `Dockerfile` confirms that the application was compiled and installed as `kripke.exe`.

Additionally, the `nodeSelector` was placed incorrectly in the manifest at `spec.pod.nodeSelector`. For the Flux Operator MiniCluster, it should be located at `spec.job.pod.spec.nodeSelector`.

The following manifest corrects these issues. It updates the command to use the correct executable name (`kripke.exe`), restores the optimization parameters from the previous attempt, sets the task count to match the number of processes, and places the `nodeSelector` in the correct location. It also adds the required `backoffLimit` and `restartPolicy`.

    # Fix 1: The executable is named kripke.exe, not kripke.
    # Re-applying optimization parameters to maximize performance.
    command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD

    # Set the backoff limit to 1 as requested
    backoffLimit: 1

        nodeSelector:

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This manifest incorporates the final corrections based on previous failures.
# 1. The executable name is set to 'kripke.exe' to resolve the "command not found" error.
# 2. The pod specification (nodeSelector, restartPolicy) is correctly placed
#    directly under `spec.pod`, which is the valid path for the v1alpha2 MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance type.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the 'kripke.exe' executable name.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy to preserve pod logs after failure.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Node selector to target the specific ARM instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

result.item:
Based on the error logs provided, I have identified two issues with the submitted Kubernetes manifest.

1.  **Command Not Found**: The container logs show the error `kripke.exe: No such file or directory` with an exit code of `127`. This indicates that the executable named `kripke.exe` cannot be found in the container's `PATH`. Although the `Dockerfile`'s `ENTRYPOINT` is set to `kripke.exe`, it's common for build systems like CMake to produce binaries without the `.exe` extension on Linux systems. The command should be `kripke`.
2.  **Incorrect Manifest Structure**: The `backoffLimit` and `pod` specifications (containing `nodeSelector` and `restartPolicy`) are placed directly under `spec`. For the `flux-framework.org/v1alpha2` `MiniCluster` custom resource, these fields should be nested under `spec.job` to correctly configure the underlying Kubernetes Job.

I have corrected these issues in the following manifest.

```yaml
# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for running Kripke.
# 1. Fixed the executable name in the command from "kripke.exe" to "kripke"
#    to resolve the "No such file or directory" error (exit code 127).
# 2. Restructured the manifest to place `backoffLimit` and `pod` specs
#    under the `job` key, as required by the MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size is the number of pods for the MiniCluster.
  size: 1
  # Tasks is the total number of MPI ranks.
  tasks: 64
  logging:

Based on the error logs, the root cause of the failure is `start failed: kripke: No such file or directory`. The container's log shows an exit code of `127`, which reinforces that the command specified was not found.

Looking at the provided Dockerfile, the application binary is installed as `kripke.exe`, but the `MiniCluster` manifest attempts to execute `kripke`.

The fix is to correct the command in the application container spec to use the correct executable name, `kripke.exe`. Additionally, the fields `backoffLimit` and `pod` were placed incorrectly in the top-level spec; they should be nested under a `job` field according to the MiniCluster specification.

  job:
    backoffLimit: 1
    pod:

        nodeSelector:

        restartPolicy: Never

    strict: true

The error `PodInitializing` combined with the series of pod recreation events strongly suggests that the pods cannot start successfully. This is often due to a mismatch between the node architecture and the container architecture, especially for the `flux-view` init container which sets up the environment. The provided manifest does not specify a node to run on, leaving the pod to be scheduled on any available node. If an ARM node is chosen by the scheduler, the default x86_64 `flux-view` init container will fail, leading to the `PodInitializing` error and subsequent pod recreation attempts.

To fix this and optimize performance as requested, I will select the most powerful CPU instance available, the `hpc7g.16xlarge` (64-core ARM), and configure the MiniCluster specifically for it. This includes setting the node selector, specifying the ARM architecture for Flux, providing the correct ARM-based image for the Flux init container, and scaling the task count and application parameters to fully utilize the node's resources. I will also add the requested `backoffLimit` and `restartPolicy`.

```yaml
# This manifest fixes the pod initialization error by explicitly selecting a node
# and ensuring all components (Flux init container, application) match the
# node's ARM architecture. It also optimizes for the "Grind Time Figure of Merit"
# by selecting the most powerful CPU instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) and scaling
# the application parameters to utilize all 64 cores.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster (1 node).
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks, set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance.
  tasks: 64
  # Ensure the pod is not cleaned up on completion to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: "arm"
    # This specific container image is required for the Flux broker on ARM nodes.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Specification for the main application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Command is optimized for a 64-task run to maximize the Figure of Merit.
      # --procs defines the MPI process grid (4x4x4 = 64).
      # --zones increases the problem size per task.
      # --nest GZD is a performance optimization for data layout.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # The main container does not need to launch flux.
      launcher: false
  
  # Specification for the underlying Kubernetes Job and Pods created by the Flux Operator.
  job:
    spec:
      # Set backoffLimit to 1 to prevent retries on persistent failures.
      backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Set restartPolicy to Never to inspect logs of failed pods.
        restartPolicy: Never
        # Selects a specific AWS instance type to ensure architecture compatibility and performance.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
```

Based on the provided error logs and manifest, I have identified two primary issues.

1.  **Incorrect Executable Name:** The error message `start failed: kripke: No such file or directory` and the corresponding exit code `127` clearly indicate that the command `kripke` cannot be found within the application container's `PATH`. Reviewing the Dockerfile shows that the installed executable is named `kripke.exe`, as specified in the `ENTRYPOINT`. The `command` in the MiniCluster spec must be changed to match this name.
2.  **Malformed Manifest Structure:** The `pod` specification, which includes the `nodeSelector`, is placed incorrectly at the top level of the `spec`. For the Flux Operator, pod-specific configurations like `nodeSelector` must be nested under `spec.job.pod.spec`. While the scheduler eventually resolved this, it is syntactically incorrect and caused initial scheduling failures.

Here is the corrected manifest that addresses these issues.

  namespace: default
spec:

  # Total number of tasks to run

  # Ensure logs are captured

    strict: true
  # Do not delete the pods after completion for debugging

    # FIX: The executable is named 'kripke.exe' per the Dockerfile. The error log

      spec:

        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

Hello! As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the provided code and error logs. Here is my assessment and the corrected manifest.

The job failed with an exit code 127, and the logs clearly state `kripke: No such file or directory`. This indicates that the command specified in the `MiniCluster` manifest could not be found within the container's PATH. Reviewing the application's Dockerfile reveals the executable is named `kripke.exe`, not `kripke`.

Additionally, the manifest has a structural error. The `pod` specification, including the `nodeSelector`, was placed directly under `spec`. For the Flux Operator, these pod-level settings must be nested under `spec.job.pod.spec`.

The corrected manifest below addresses these issues. It also incorporates the required `backoffLimit` and `restartPolicy` settings and re-applies the optimization parameters from the previous step to align with the goal of maximizing performance.

```yaml

kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The size of the MiniCluster (number of pods) is 1, as required.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks must match the MPI processes requested in the command.
  # --procs 4,4,4 requests 4*4*4=64 processes. The previous run used 1, which was not optimal.
  tasks: 64

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Specify the application container.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke

    # The previous command "kripke" resulted in a "No such file or directory" error.
    # Re-instating optimization parameters to maximize performance.
    command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD

    launcher: false

    backoffLimit: 1
    # The pod spec was incorrectly placed at the top level of the MiniCluster spec.
    # It must be nested under job.pod.spec for the operator to parse it correctly.
    pod:

          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

    strict: true
  
  # Cleanup is set to false to allow for log inspection on failure.
  cleanup: false

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This manifest incorporates the final corrections based on previous failures.
# 1. The executable name is set to 'kripke.exe' to resolve the "command not found" error.
# 2. The pod specification (nodeSelector, restartPolicy) is correctly placed
#    directly under `spec.pod`, which is the valid path for the v1alpha2 MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods for the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of tasks is set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance type.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete the pods and services upon job completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Specifies the number of retries before considering a Job as failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation of this manifest.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected the command to use the 'kripke.exe' executable name.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # This container is a worker, not a dedicated launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Flux-specific configuration for the ARM architecture of the selected node.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"

  # Defines pod-level specifications.
  pod:
    # Specifies the restart policy to preserve pod logs after failure.
    restartPolicy: "Never"
    # Node selector to target the specific ARM instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"

result.item:
Based on the error logs provided, I have identified two issues with the submitted Kubernetes manifest.

1.  **Command Not Found**: The container logs show the error `kripke.exe: No such file or directory` with an exit code of `127`. This indicates that the executable named `kripke.exe` cannot be found in the container's `PATH`. Although the `Dockerfile`'s `ENTRYPOINT` is set to `kripke.exe`, it's common for build systems like CMake to produce binaries without the `.exe` extension on Linux systems. The command should be `kripke`.
2.  **Incorrect Manifest Structure**: The `backoffLimit` and `pod` specifications (containing `nodeSelector` and `restartPolicy`) are placed directly under `spec`. For the `flux-framework.org/v1alpha2` `MiniCluster` custom resource, these fields should be nested under `spec.job` to correctly configure the underlying Kubernetes Job.

I have corrected these issues in the following manifest.

```yaml
# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for running Kripke.
# 1. Fixed the executable name in the command from "kripke.exe" to "kripke"
#    to resolve the "No such file or directory" error (exit code 127).
# 2. Restructured the manifest to place `backoffLimit` and `pod` specs
#    under the `job` key, as required by the MiniCluster CRD.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size is the number of pods for the MiniCluster.
  size: 1
  # Tasks is the total number of MPI ranks.
  tasks: 64
  logging:
    strict: true
  cleanup: false

  # Application container to run.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # Corrected executable name. The error "kripke.exe: No such file or directory" indicates
    # the binary is likely named 'kripke' on the Linux file system.
    command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
    launcher: false

  # Flux RESTful API settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # JobSpec to control the underlying Kubernetes Job.
  job:
    # Limit retries to 1. If it fails once, it will not be retried.
    backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Select the ARM-based instance type for this workload.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
        # Do not restart pods on failure so logs can be inspected.
        restartPolicy: Never
```

result.item:
The error `PodInitializing` combined with the series of pod recreation events strongly suggests that the pods cannot start successfully. This is often due to a mismatch between the node architecture and the container architecture, especially for the `flux-view` init container which sets up the environment. The provided manifest does not specify a node to run on, leaving the pod to be scheduled on any available node. If an ARM node is chosen by the scheduler, the default x86_64 `flux-view` init container will fail, leading to the `PodInitializing` error and subsequent pod recreation attempts.

To fix this and optimize performance as requested, I will select the most powerful CPU instance available, the `hpc7g.16xlarge` (64-core ARM), and configure the MiniCluster specifically for it. This includes setting the node selector, specifying the ARM architecture for Flux, providing the correct ARM-based image for the Flux init container, and scaling the task count and application parameters to fully utilize the node's resources. I will also add the requested `backoffLimit` and `restartPolicy`.

```yaml
# This manifest fixes the pod initialization error by explicitly selecting a node
# and ensuring all components (Flux init container, application) match the
# node's ARM architecture. It also optimizes for the "Grind Time Figure of Merit"
# by selecting the most powerful CPU instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) and scaling
# the application parameters to utilize all 64 cores.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods in the MiniCluster (1 node).
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks, set to match the vCPU count of the selected instance.
  tasks: 64
  # Ensure the pod is not cleaned up on completion to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific settings for ARM architecture.
  flux:
    arch: "arm"
    # This specific container image is required for the Flux broker on ARM nodes.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Specification for the main application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Command is optimized for a 64-task run to maximize the Figure of Merit.
      # --procs defines the MPI process grid (4x4x4 = 64).
      # --zones increases the problem size per task.
      # --nest GZD is a performance optimization for data layout.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --zones 96,96,96 --nest GZD
      # The main container does not need to launch flux.
      launcher: false
  
  # Specification for the underlying Kubernetes Job and Pods created by the Flux Operator.
  job:
    spec:
      # Set backoffLimit to 1 to prevent retries on persistent failures.
      backoffLimit: 1
    pod:
      spec:
        # Set restartPolicy to Never to inspect logs of failed pods.
        restartPolicy: Never
        # Selects a specific AWS instance type to ensure architecture compatibility and performance.
        nodeSelector:
          node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
```
